newsitem.title: GERMANY: Economist sees need for gene-altered grain crops.
newsitem.headline: Economist sees need for gene-altered grain crops.

text.p: Grain producers need to explore genetically modified crops to achieve yields that will match expanding demand, economist Rudolf Stoehr of grain trader Toepfer said.
Of the extra grain needed to meet world demand in the years to 2020, some 80 percent would have to come from yield rises, he told a seminar during the "Green Week" farm fair.
This assumed existing land and water reserves were being used.
Stoehr calculated grain supply additions between 1995 and 2020 from the deployment of additional land reserves and higher yields at 1.7 percent per year on average.
But he put likely demand rises from population growth and increased spending power at 2.0 or 2.5 percent each year.
The developing deficits would not be strongly felt until the next century, he said.
World grain output in 1996/97 would be adequate again at 1.45 billion tonnes, up eight percent from a tight 1995/96 season, so stocks could be rebuilt.
Wheat prices rallies as seen in the spring of 1996 were a thing of the past, at least for now.
Current world market prices around $155 a tonne fob compared with $190 a year ago and a peak of $250-260 last April.
